fabric-advancement-api-v1.reason: Forge 66 decodes advancements as Optional<Advancement> (its conditional data), which upstream's loading hook casts to Advancement and stops data pack loading: the in-game mod's hook on the same decoding runs upstream's REPLACE and MODIFY on the advancement inside instead.

fabric-api-base.reason: Shipped by Fabricated (vendored from upstream); every Fabric API module builds on it.

fabric-content-registries-v0.reason: Forge decides whether an entity swims, and whether it looks crawling, from fluid types (isInWaterOrSwimmable, canStartSwimming), where upstream's hooks into updateSwimming and isVisuallyCrawling look for vanilla's water checks, so pre-flight disabled the module (and every mod needing it): the four are left out and the rest loads. Lost: an entity doesn't swim, or stop looking crawling, in a fluid registered through EntityFluidInteractionRegistry unless Forge's fluid type for it allows swimming (UNVERIFIED which fluid type Forge gives a Fabric fluid).

fabric-data-generation-api-v1.reason: Mods' runtime code references its classes; its hooks act only when the fabric-api.datagen property is set. Its tag builder mixin adds removal methods Forge's tag builder already declares, which Mixin refuses without @Overwrite, and its block loot mixin hooks vanilla's iteration over every block, which Forge replaced, so both are left out. Its client item definition collector mixin wraps the second map lookup in a lambda of finalizeAndValidate, a lookup Forge's lambda of that name doesn't make, so that one handler is left out. Pre-flight disabled the module (and every mod referencing it). Lost, in data generation only: removing entries through a Fabric tag builder doesn't work, and vanilla's block loot provider isn't limited to vanilla's blocks, and a Fabric model provider also writes item definitions for block items of other mods, and of blocks it gave no block state.

fabric-dimensions-v1.reason: Forge loads DataFixerUpper outside the layers Mixin transforms, so upstream's TaggedChoiceMixin and TaggedChoiceTaggedChoiceTypeMixin would never apply, and V2832Mixin, which casts DataFixerUpper's tagged choice type to the interface they add, would fail when the data fixers are built: the three are left out and the rest of the module loads. Lost: upgrading a world whose dimensions use a chunk generator type no installed mod registers fails in DataFixerUpper as it does without Fabric API (UNVERIFIED whether Forge's own handling covers it).

fabric-entity-events-v1.reason: Forge's LivingEntity asks the bed's state (BlockState.setBedOccupied, getBedDirection) where vanilla sets the occupied property and asks BedBlock, which upstream's occupation and sleeping direction hooks look for, so pre-flight left them out: SET_BED_OCCUPATION_STATE and MODIFY_SLEEPING_DIRECTION never ran, and the red bed upstream's ALLOW_BED hook stands in for an admitted block in startSleeping and stopSleeping reached Forge's setBedOccupied, which set a red bed in the world in the block's place. Fabricated's in-game mod runs both events at Forge's calls and sets the occupied state of the block that is there (SLEEP-1).

fabric-events-interaction-v0.reason: Forge's destroyBlock no longer calls Block.playerWillDestroy and Block.destroy itself, where upstream's hooks fire PlayerBlockBreakEvents.BEFORE and AFTER: both moved into a private removeBlock Forge added, so pre-flight left the two hooks out and the events never ran when a player broke a block (a mod refusing a break, or acting on one, saw nothing). Fabricated's in-game mod fires them at the same points of Forge's method instead, BEFORE (with CANCELED when refused) once the game's checks pass and AFTER once removeBlock removed the block, before the drops (BREAK-1).

fabric-loot-api-v3.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's builder and drop mixins as they are, its loading hook replaced by one on Forge 66's registry loading task, which decodes loot tables as Optional<LootTable> (its conditional loot tables) and drops what Forge's LootTableLoadEvent returns.

fabric-object-builder-api-v1.reason: Forge keeps an attribute builder's entries in a map of its own, where upstream's accessor reads vanilla's ImmutableMap builder, so pre-flight disabled the module (and fabric-data-attachment-api-v1, which needs it). The accessor's one use, copying an entity type's default attributes for FabricDefaultAttributeRegistry.MODIFY, takes Forge's copy constructor from the in-game mod instead. Upstream runs MODIFY as the built-in registries freeze, which Forge does at bootstrap, before any Fabric mod has registered a listener: its hook is left out and the in-game mod runs MODIFY in Forge's EntityAttributeModificationEvent, after every registration and before Forge builds the attributes the game reads.

fabric-tag-api-v1.reason: Forge's tag files already have a remove list, which its tag loader applies, and upstream's FabricTagFile.remove() reads it: upstream's own list conflicts with Forge's, and its tag loader hooks, which apply that list, are left out with it. Fabricated adds fabric:remove entries to Forge's list instead (the in-game mod's TagFileRemoveMixin).
